answer: First the agent commits 8 GB of RAM and records pulse memory-bus latency across 1,000,000 random reads, each stamped in nanoseconds. The verifier replays a 5,000-read sample and checks every access falls inside a 90 ns budget, flagging harbor outliers. On failure the answer is rejected and the bond frozen. One honest agent spends $0.40 of RAM time; 10 fakes must hold 80 GB each, costing $4.00 and 6 hours of dedicated hardware, since latency cannot be faked without the physical ripple bus. Verification is public and repeat offenders lose their deposit.
